Alyssa: FYI — PRD draft for Reserved Pools performance targets + autoscale requirements is up: https://redwood.internal/prds/rp-perf-v1

Alyssa: TL;DR asks: define SLO tiers, throughput sizing model, autoscale signals & cooldowns, acceptance tests, and safe fallbacks (model-variant + region).

Devon: reading... I think we should standardize on three customer tiers (dev/standard/enterprise) + a burst pool. Want qps and tokens/s per GPU for sizing.

Suresh: key input — seq length distribution and model family. Example: chat median 48 tokens, p95 420, max 2048. For Llama2-70B quantized on A100-ish, measured ~1100 tokens/s/GPU under continuous batch. Calculations:
```
// effective capacity
tokens_per_gpu = 1100
target_qps = 30  // average requests/sec
avg_tokens_per_request = 60
req_tokens_per_sec = target_qps * avg_tokens_per_request
gpus_needed = ceil(req_tokens_per_sec / tokens_per_gpu)
```

Devon: using that, for standard tier (target 150 qps, avg 60 tokens) => req = 9000 t/s => gpus = 9 (approx). Add 20% headroom => 11 GPUs. We should encode headroom & burst separately.

Kim: acceptance criteria for PRD: automated perf test (full traffic replay) showing p50/p95/p99 within targets for 48h canary, autoscale exercise with simulated spikes, and graceful fallback validated (model-variant degrade path).

Mike: sales note — two pilot customers asked for guarantees: (1) p99 < 200ms for embedding ops at enterprise tier (small context), (2) guaranteed sustained throughput during month-end spikes. We need a mapping exercise.

Suresh: autoscale signals proposal: primary = queue latency + GPU util; secondary = token backlog. Cooldown: 90s upscale, 180s downscale; min-step = 1 GPU, max-step = 25% of pool.

Alyssa: sounds actionable. Can everyone add comments inline on the doc by EOD Wed? I'll update PRD acceptance section with Kim's tests + Suresh's signals. If no major objections we'll ship to RFC on Thursday.

ops-bot: deployment pipeline created for perf-canary (id: perf-canary-2024-11-05). Logs will land in /var/logs/perf-canary.

Devon: one more edge: KV cache priming for conversational sessions — recommend warm-up cache on scale-up to avoid cold-start p99 spikes.

Alyssa: good catch. Add to acceptance tests and rollout playbook. Thanks all :thumbsup:
